newsitem.title: USA: US FAA awards Raytheon contract up to $44 mln.
newsitem.headline: US FAA awards Raytheon contract up to $44 mln.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration on Wednesday awarded Raytheon Co a contract worth up to $44.5 million for a weather prediction system to cover airspace within about 60 miles of an airport.
Acting FAA Administrator Linda Daschle said "We believe this system will be a significant step toward avoiding delays caused by threatening weather and increasing the margin of safety."

The FAA said the system, using FAA and national weather service data, would generate predictions of weather phenomena such as microbursts, gust fronts, storm cell movements and runway winds up to 10 minutes in advance.

It said the system would also display data on the presence of lightning, hail and tornados, information that is critical during takeoffs and landings when weather hazards pose the greatest danger to aircraft.

The FAA said Raytheon would develop, test, install and maintain units to cover 45 airports with significant weather hazards. It said the first unit would be operational at Memphis, Tenn., in November 2001, and the last at Dayton, Ohio, in February 2003.
